blocks.text: An API key is required for authenticating with the ZPA API to make API calls.
If you need to obtain API keys or secrets to access Zscaler OneAPI endpoints, see API Client Authentication in Authentication Service.
To add a new API key:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > API > Private Access API.

If you are subscribed to Authentication Service and have it enabled for your tenant, API keys created in Authentication Service appear on the API Keys page in the Zscaler Admin Console and are read only. To learn more, see What Is Authentication Service?
The Add API Keys drawer opens.
In the Add API Keys drawer:
Name: Enter a name for the key.
Status: Enable the key. If Disabled, the key will be unavailable to use. By default, this is enabled.
Session Validity Interval (In Seconds): The amount of time the key is available to use. The maximum amount of time is 3,600 seconds.

Role: The predefined role or a custom role of the API key (e.g., API Read Only, API Full Access). Roles for API keys enforce granular role-based access control (RBAC) on all publicly available ZPA API operations. For each API key, you can select the API Full Access predefined role to provide full access to the Private Access API. To learn more, see Understanding Role-Based Access Control for Private Access API, About API Clients, and Adding an API Client.
The client secret for the key is displayed.
Copy the client secret to your clipboard. You will need it for authentication.
The client secret is only available to copy when creating an API key. It is not available to access in the Zscaler Admin Console after you close the drawer, so store it in a secure location.
